source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)

coverage.scope: Whole-chapter master decision framework and independent calculations (avoid/recover/preserve, secured waterfall, state present creditor, fraud value, preference dividends, subsequent new value, floating liens, setoff insufficiency, Ponzi net winners), 13-case map; no original textbook problem answered

topics.title: Chapter 9 Exam Roadmap: Classify Avoidance Power Before Calculating
topics.description: Which statute fits what transfer, what date, what beneficiary and what defense?

entries.title: Step 1: identify transaction and affected estate interest
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Was debtor's own property transferred prepetition, lien imperfectly perfected, asset gifted/sold, old creditor paid, account netted, or collateral seized postpetition? Identify transferor, recipient, consideration and petition timeline.
entries.laymanExplanation: Different conduct activates different lawsuit.
entries.legalExplanation: §544(a) priority; §544(b)/§548 fraudulent transfers; §547 preference; §549 unauthorized postpetition; §553 prepetition setoff; §550 recovery and §551 preservation.
entries.examApplication: Write transaction flowchart and dates before legal conclusions.
entries.examTrap: Cannot use all avoidance statutes interchangeably.

entries.title: Step 2: select law and standing
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: §544(a): hypothetical petition-date lien creditor/execution creditor/BFP; §544(b): ACTUAL allowable unsecured creditor qualified under state law; §548: trustee federal statutory power; §547: trustee preference; DIP under §1107(a) usually trustee analogue.
entries.laymanExplanation: For (a), pretend claimant exists; for (b), find a real creditor.
entries.legalExplanation: Keep state transfer law vs federal Code source distinct, verify ordinary limitation/transaction types.
entries.examApplication: State actual creditor, timing and governing state law.
entries.examTrap: Borrowing §544(b) still requires someone with an allowable unsecured claim.

entries.title: Step 3: distinguish voidability, recipient liability, recovered value
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Apply underlying avoiding power; after invalidation, §550 identifies first legal transferee, benefited guarantor, protected subsequent buyer and §550(d) single satisfaction; §502(h) claim may revive; §551 saves avoided lien priority.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judicial declaration not itself cash; need proper recovery defendant.
entries.legalExplanation: Video Depot, Railworks and Moore v Bay illustrate special consequences.
entries.examApplication: Draw transfer arrows and title/benefit separately.
entries.examTrap: Mere conduit never identical to first recipient legal dominion.

entries.title: Step 4: public title snapshot or intent/value analysis
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: For §544(a), ask UCC/realty recording priority at petition, 20-day purchase-money relation-back etc. For §544(b)/§548, ask debtor property, state triggering creditor, actual intent badges OR value deficiency plus qualifying financial condition, recovery defenses.
entries.laymanExplanation: A secret UCC lien is different from insolvent gift; evaluate accordingly.
entries.legalExplanation: Costas property disclaimer, Omegas equitable remedy and BFP foreclosure illustrate property definitions and exceptions.
entries.examApplication: Name selected theory first, then prove each element.
entries.examTrap: Avoid presuming hindsight bad outcome demonstrates no equivalent value.

entries.title: Step 5: §547 preference -> defendant §547(c) safe harbors
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Trustee establishes seven preference elements including creditor, antecedent debt, insolvency, 90-day/insider year and better-than-Ch7. THEN recipient may prove ordinary-course, contemporaneous/new value, enabling loan, floating lien or other defense.
entries.laymanExplanation: Payment on real old invoice can be attacked, but ordinary trade payment may be safe.
entries.legalExplanation: Do not blend §547(c)(3) 30-day enabling with UCC §9-317(e) 20-day strong-arm exception.
entries.examApplication: Use stepwise burden chart and defendant timeline.
entries.examTrap: Creditor's insolvency knowledge not prima facie requirement.

entries.title: Step 6: §553 setoff or recoupment, avoid confusing with preference
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Setoff requires two-way same-capacity PREpetition mutual debt and state entitlement, subject §362 stay and §553(a)(2)/(3) conditions; ACTUAL setoff before petition invokes §553(b) two-point insufficiency. Recoupment can span petition if same integrated transaction.
entries.laymanExplanation: Same person owing each other money can net, but different affiliate or new purchase often cannot.
entries.legalExplanation: SemCrude, insurer/publisher and Banjo Problem9.15 fact patterns.
entries.examApplication: Track distinct persons/capacities and two date balances.
entries.examTrap: A right to pay less via triangular offset isn't automatically independent §101(5) claim.

entries.title: Step 7: Ponzi alternative claims and net-winner division
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Use §548 actual presumption for fraudulent scheme, §548 constructive no-value fake profits, §548(c) principal value/good faith, §547 90-day principal payments/ordinary course; no free-floating universal equity power.
entries.laymanExplanation: Winner's paid fictitious interest different from getting one's original cash back.
entries.legalExplanation: Independent Clearing House and Cunningham compared.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish claim size, net return, good faith, legal lookback.
entries.examTrap: Net loser may still face preference on recent principal repayment.

entries.title: Step 8: judicial opinion versus book challenge
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Case holding is only one piece: book critiques Omegas/Costas property definitions, BFP Scalia-v-Souter state deference, Marshall borrowing substitution, National Gas ordinary industry standard, Railworks conduit liability and SemCrude nonrecourse guarantee.
entries.laymanExplanation: Professor may ask 'why should the case have come out differently?'
entries.legalExplanation: Make two-sided analysis but label actual holding, dissent and textbook critique.
entries.examApplication: Use relevant precise source facts and statutory terms.
entries.examTrap: Don't rewrite historical cases to pretend amended law existed then.

topics.title: Chapter 9 Calculations: All Formula Types and Worked Independent Examples
topics.description: Source-preserving mathematical practice without answering original Problems9.1–9.15.

entries.title: Lien preservation §551 collateral waterfall
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Collateral $52,000, avoided senior lien securing $17,000, junior lien securing $80,000: estate occupies former senior $17k priority and residual collateral $35k available to junior; junior still has unsecured deficiency.
entries.laymanExplanation: Avoiding senior doesn't hand its priority slot to junior.
entries.legalExplanation: Amount captured is lesser of avoided lien priority and realizable collateral, subject other interests.
entries.examApplication: Draw senior estate first, junior second.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply $10k/$20k textbook example as user's unsolved assignment outcome.

entries.title: Moore v Bay triggering creditor vs whole transfer
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Total estate unsecured $70k, property wrongfully transferred $26k, one eligible actual creditor only $250: if §544(b) claim properly establishes avoidable transaction, entire $26k transfer may be avoided and shared estate-wide, not capped $250.
entries.laymanExplanation: One small real creditor unlocks whole recovery.
entries.legalExplanation: Separate state-law creditor standing from estate recoverable transfer and shared distribution.
entries.examApplication: Model money flow; preserve original Problem9.1 unsolved.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume UVTA individual creditor §7 itself gives full 26k personal recovery.

entries.title: §548 constructively fraudulent value gap
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: A debtor with $90k assets and $130k debts gifts a $12k machine for $3k: nominal value shortfall $9k; evaluate whether $3k cash actually retained/returned, §548(c) credit, and transfer vs recovery separately.
entries.laymanExplanation: Giving $12k for $3k while insolvent removes $9k value before creditor relief.
entries.legalExplanation: Difference suggests insufficient equivalence but formal remedy can involve whole transfer subject defenses.
entries.examApplication: Do not jump from shortfall arithmetic to full recipient personal liability.
entries.examTrap: Economically different from selling at reasonable market value then hiding proceeds with actual intent.

entries.title: §547(b)(5) more-than-liquidation comparison formula
entries.page: Ch9 E / Palmer Clay independent example
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: If unsecured creditor has $24k original claim, receives $6k before filing, and Ch7 pays remaining unsecured claims 30%, with payment kept gets $6k+0.30×$18k=$11.4k; without payment gets 0.30×$24k=$7.2k. Improvement $4.2k = $6k×(1−0.30).
entries.laymanExplanation: Early $6k plus dividend on remaining invoice beats simple 30% claim payout.
entries.legalExplanation: Illustrative simplified fixed-dividend assumption, actual Chapter7 pool may be recalculated.
entries.examApplication: For fully-secured or partly secured claims compute secured portions first.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply unsecured algebra mechanically to original secured Problem9.11.

entries.title: §547(c)(4) subsequent NEW value running ledger
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Start avoidable prefiling old debt payment $12,000; creditor then ships NEW $4,500 unsecured inventory and then another $2,000 on credit, both after preference and qualifying, no disqualifying repayment: provisional net vulnerable amount $12,000−$4,500−$2,000=$5,500, subject statutory details.
entries.laymanExplanation: Fresh goods given after a preference offset previous favored payment.
entries.legalExplanation: Order controls: if goods precede payment, not subsequent new value for that payment.
entries.examApplication: Mark each payment vs shipment +/− in dates grid.
entries.examTrap: This is NOT worked answer to original Problem9.12.

entries.title: PMSI clock comparison: UCC20 vs federal §547(c)(3)30
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Debtor receives new financed tool day0, files bankruptcy day10; lender files public financing day18: analyze UCC relation-back ≤20 days for §544 and independent §547 enabling-loan ≤30 days. For filing day25, don't confuse Code30 with UCC20.
entries.laymanExplanation: One document deadline protects a fictional lien creditor, another protects from preference.
entries.legalExplanation: Need separate statutory facts and time of transfer under §547(e).
entries.examApplication: Use separate test grids.
entries.examTrap: Exact grace period may vary by collateral/statute; examples source simple goods.

entries.title: §547(c)(5) floating lien two-point deficiency
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Day90 lender claim $150k, inventory $105k → deficiency $45k. Petition claim $150k, inventory $127k → deficiency $23k. Improvement $22k, potentially avoidable if security/value conditions satisfied.
entries.laymanExplanation: Lender became $22k more secured without new money.
entries.legalExplanation: Two-point look at unsecured shortfall, floor zero; inventory turnover does not itself equal preference.
entries.examApplication: For original Problem9.14 preserve numerical subparts.
entries.examTrap: Don't use June15 low point rather than statutory endpoints.

entries.title: §553(b) insufficiency two-point
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Day90 bank claim $40k, bank owes depositor $12k → insufficiency $28k. Day of actual prefiling setoff claim $40k and bank debt $25k → insufficiency $15k. Improvement $13k potential §553(b) recovery; remaining claim restored under §502(h).
entries.laymanExplanation: Bigger customer deposits make old bank claim more collectible.
entries.legalExplanation: Unlike §553(a)(3), §553(b) does not require purpose or insolvency proof.
entries.examApplication: Always use date of actual setoff, not petition if different.
entries.examTrap: If no prefiling setoff, apply (a)/(stay) instead.

entries.title: §553(a) straightforward netting and mutuality
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: D owes C $4,200 for accounting while C owes D $5,000 for goods, same capacities both prepetition: valid setoff if nonbankruptcy law permits up to $4,200, estate receives $800; if amounts owed by C's subsidiary, no ordinary mutuality.
entries.laymanExplanation: Only remaining balance crosses table.
entries.legalExplanation: Find underlying contract right and §362 permission if after petition.
entries.examApplication: Keep distinct debtors' balances and capacities.
entries.examTrap: This does not solve original banjo Problem9.15.

entries.title: Ponzi gross receipts, contributed principal and fake net profits
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: An investor contributed $30k total and withdrew $37k before filing; net gain $7k. Candidate constructive fake-profit portion up to $7k; $30k return of principal can extinguish restitution debt and be protected if good faith/value. Actual fraud theory and §547 timing can still affect principal.
entries.laymanExplanation: Paid winnings beyond cash invested is different from reimbursement.
entries.legalExplanation: Use aggregate amounts per beneficiary and analyze temporal accounting under controlling law.
entries.examApplication: Don't assume 100% of $37k automatically collectible.
entries.examTrap: Recipient good faith separate question; avoid double recovery §550(d).

entries.title: Chomakos ex ante payoff versus creditor limited liability
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: For RANDOM gamble, expected gamble gross payout = sum(probability×payoff). But creditor expected recovery ≈ sum(probability×MIN(payoff, creditor claim)), and debtor expected residual ≈ sum(probability×MAX(0,payoff−creditor claim)). Example stake $6k, debts $8k, win $12k with 50%: gross expectation $6k; creditor capped expectation $4k; debtor residual expectation $2k. Compare no-bet $6k available to creditors, debtor $0.
entries.laymanExplanation: A fair-dollar lottery can lower creditor expected collection even if debtor sees chance of personal upside.
entries.legalExplanation: Illustrative ONLY, expressly NOT answering original $10k/$12k Chomakos exercise.
entries.examApplication: Write separate probability columns; show bankruptcy limited liability.
entries.examTrap: Value-in-exchange law not automatically creditor-welfare expected-recovery rule.

topics.title: Chapter 9 Thirteen Full Cases: Issue and Contrast Map
topics.description: Fast way to recall the assigned opinions by their controlling question.

entries.title: All thirteen full source excerpts in chapter order
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Video Depot (§550 initial transferee/cashier check); Railworks (conduit not beneficiary on agency liability); Omegas (unimposed constructive trust); Costas (prepetition inheritance disclaimer); Alan Drey (actual intent/red flag buyer); BFP (regular foreclosure price safe harbor, 4-justice dissent); Chomakos (ex ante lawful gambling value); Cunningham (Ponzi victim tracing/§547); Marshall (credit card loan proceeds/earmarking); Palmer Clay (§547(b)(5) dividend); National Gas (objective ordinary-course defense); SemCrude (triangular setoff mutuality); Independent Clearing House (Ponzi principal vs profits/presumption).
entries.laymanExplanation: Each case supplies a distinct doctrinal fork.
entries.legalExplanation: All 13 have separate full case brief note with facts, issue, holding, reasoning, rule.
entries.examApplication: Choose closest two and contrast.
entries.examTrap: Don't brief Moore v Bay/Twyne/Belisle as full opinions absent excerpts.

entries.title: Contrasts that resolve exam confusion
entries.source: User-supplied Bankruptcy Chapter9 §§A–G synthesis, derived independent study aids (no original numbered problems solved)
entries.summary: Video Depot legal dominion of recipient vs Marshall debtor control of borrowed loan proceeds; Railworks mere conduit vs genuine guarantor beneficiary; Omegas general trust skepticism vs Cunningham traced victim money; Costas deference vs BFP federalism; BFP forced realty value vs Chomakos chance value; National Gas vs Independent Ponzi ordinary course; SemCrude setoff vs actual distinct guarantee.
entries.laymanExplanation: Same vocabulary 'dominion' or 'value' does not mean same test.
entries.legalExplanation: Identify which statute and whose property right is at stake.
entries.examApplication: Use this comparison as final paragraph after applying relevant Code element.
entries.examTrap: Do not extrapolate lower-court holding to universal rule without procedural context.
